cribl-decision-2.code_revision: THE AUTHOR'S OWN MODEL AND DECISION LIBRARY, with a first-party System One wire shim: cribl-ai/cribl-decision-2 at 92ac09eccd2a3c24d41ad31e659e4d681261b57b. The author supplies a library, no HTTP server. The first-party wire shim adds loopback /health and /v1/systemone, exactly one frozen decision per request. It passes the state as text (JSON with ensure_ascii=False for structured state), instructions, original criteria and type to the unmodified author Question/decide_batch([question], batch_size=1). Noul maps to author boolean with false/true criteria preserved; choice keys, order and descriptions remain native. Score uses the full native ordered level distribution, re-keyed to frozen zero-based index strings, including duplicate level text; the author's one-based expected value is not the wire result. No synthetic probabilities, prompt cropping, averaging, extra decision pass, generator or quantization. Full fine-tuned weights and decision heads, not a LoRA adapter. Native decision.py preserves bidirectional full attention, learned reverse linear scans and option-marker readout; batch size one, BF16 on CUDA, one complete native decision pass. The complete rendered prompt cap is 4,096 tokens, checked by the author's code before forward, with no truncation. Only the exact native over-limit ValueError, with independently observed prompt length over 4,096, maps to HTTP 422; other inference/framework/OOM/marker faults remain HTTP 500. Author prompt generation and tokenization remain unchanged, including chat template, special-token neutralization with U+2060, tokenizer(text)'s default special-token behavior, assistant header and empty think block. First-party rendering is for offline counting only. Public pod probes compared complete token-ID lists with the actual native prompt and compared native/shim distributions before sealed input. USAGE IS FIRST-PARTY WIRE ACCOUNTING: successful input usage is the complete native tokenized prompt length, output_tokens 0 for classifier readout; a known native pre-forward refusal has input_tokens 0 and output_tokens 0. This is not an author-native API billing contract. The frozen TypeSafe adapter and measurement driver are unchanged; no answer repair, host retry, prompt rewrite or ensemble. decide-1.1.author: decide.sh (paid priority evaluation, public)
decide-1.1.cost_basis: API launch list price (I-1): https://decide.sh/pricing, applied since 2026-10-29. USD 0.03 per million input tokens; output free (input-only billing), no base model declared and no override.
decide-1.1.disclosure: FIRST MEASUREMENT (paid priority evaluation). NOUL FLOOR: by vendor default decide-1.1 reports an unsure yes/no answer at 0.801 (yes side) or 0.199 (no side), so no noul answer lies between 0.2 and 0.8; the vendor documents this default as its benchmark mode and the raw calibrated mode ('noul_floor': false) as not meant for benchmark runs. Measured at the vendor default; 61 of 375 noul answers sit exactly at 0.801/0.199. Choice and score answers are unaffected. LONG INPUTS: the vendor documents a 50,000-character document limit; the 5 items of this draw above that limit were all answered (HTTP 200), so they are scored as answered. Before the run these 5 positions had been pre-registered as expected HTTP 413 misses; custody amended that pre-registration because of the outcome (all answered), not the score. RETRIES: 2 requests returned a transient HTTP 503 ('the decision model didn't answer, try again') and were answered on the harness's single documented retry. Hosting implementation and deployed weights were not independently inspected; no weights are published. LIMITS: the vendor documents a 25-second request limit (HTTP 503 after it). HARNESS: the measurement client follows HTTP redirects as standard; every answer carried the vendor's model id decide-1.1.

iota-decide-4b-v0.4.disclosure: FIRST MEASUREMENT of v0.4 (paid priority evaluation). FAMILY: new checkpoint of a family with earlier rows on an earlier draw (iota-decide-4b, iota-decide-4b-v0.3); new weights, no weight file shared. CONTEXT: prompts longer than 16,384 tokens are cut by the model (letter_decide.fit_state keeps the head and tail of the state) and answered (5 items on this draw; scored as answered).
